results.title: Authentication
results.snippet:
The Gemini Notebook API uses [OAuth 2.0](https://developers.google.com/identity/protocols/oauth2) to authenticate requests on behalf of a Google user. Every request must include an OAuth 2.0 Bearer token in the `Authorization` HTTP header. The API doesn't accept API keys.

- **Use a personal Google Account.** During the Public Preview, the Gemini Notebook API is only available for personal Google Accounts. Requests authenticated with a Google Workspace account fail with `403 PERMISSION_DENIED` (`WORKSPACE_ACCOUNT_NOT_SUPPORTED`).
- **Sign in to Gemini Notebook once.** The API reads and writes the notebooks of the authorizing user, so each Google Account must have signed in to [Gemini Notebook](https://notebook.google.com) at least once before calling the API. If an account has never signed in to Gemini Notebook, `CreateNotebook` requests fail with `404 NOT_FOUND` (`Account not found for user.`).
## OAuth 2.0 scopes
Requests must be authenticated with an OAuth 2.0 token granted one of the following scopes:
| Scope | Access | Supported methods |
|---|---|---|
| `https://www.googleapis.com/auth/notebook` | Read and write access to notebooks and sources | `CreateNotebook`, `GetNotebook

results.title: Gemini Notebook (formerly NotebookLM) API: Key and Pricing
results.snippet:
No, not for personal accounts. Google’s only documented Gemini Notebook API belongs to Gemini Notebook Enterprise on Google Cloud, and its setup steps require Enterprise licenses before you make a single call ([Google Cloud](https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/notebooklm-enterprise/docs/api-notebooks), 2026). Free, Plus, Pro and Ultra accounts have nothing official to call. As a result, every consumer integration you’ll find works around the app, not through it.

**The Gemini Notebook Enterprise API** is Google’s v1alpha API for notebooks in the Google Cloud edition. It manages notebooks, sources and audio, but it doesn’t chat. Google’s docs list methods to create, get, list recently viewed, delete and share notebooks, add or upload sources, and create or delete audio overviews (Google Cloud, 2026). Specifically, every call goes to a v1alpha endpoint under Google’s Pre-GA terms, which “might have limited support”. In addition, calls carry an OAuth access token from `gcloud auth print-access-token`. That’s why there’s no “NotebookLM API key” to copy from a settings page.

Access costs money and admin work. Google’s product page lists Gemini Notebook for Enterprise at $9

results.title: Get licenses for Gemini Notebook Enterprise
results.snippet:
There are two subscription *tiers* for Gemini Notebook Enterprise:
- **The free-trial tier:** With this tier, you get a full-featured, 14-day trial subscription of 5000 licenses.
- **The paid tier:** You can buy a monthly subscription or a year-long subscription. Both the monthly and the yearly subscriptions can be set to renew automatically.
## Before you begin
Before starting the procedures on this page, make sure that:
- You have completed the tasks on the [Set up Gemini Notebook Enterprise](https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/notebooklm-enterprise/docs/set-up-notebooklm). This includes granting at least the **Cloud NotebookLM User** (`roles/discoveryengine.notebookLmUser`) role to any users who you'll license to use Gemini Notebook Enterprise (including free-trial users).
- You have the following roles:
- Cloud NotebookLM Admin (`roles/discoveryengine.notebookLmOwner`)
- Gemini Enterprise Admin (`roles/discoveryengine.agentspaceAdmin`)

## Use the US multi-regional endpoint
If your Gemini Notebook Enterprise subscription is in the US multi-region, you can send the requests on this page to the US multi-regional endpoint, `discoveryengine.us.rep.googleapis.com`. A multi-regional endpoint processes your requests and terminates TLS within the multi-region, so your request data stays in the US while it's in transit. Using this endpoint doesn't change where your notebooks are stored. For more information, see [Regional and multi-regional API endpoints overview](https://docs.cloud.google.com/docs/security/compliance/about-regional-endpoints) in the Google Cloud security guide.

To add sources to a notebook, call the [`notebooks.sources.batchCreate`](https://docs.cloud.google.com/gemini/enterprise/docs/reference/rest/v1alpha/projects.locations.notebooks.sources/batchCreate) method.

results.snippet:
Model Context Protocol (MCP) server that provides Agent Platform tools for building, deploying, and scaling both predictive machine learning and generative AI applications on Google Cloud.
A [Model Context Protocol (MCP) server](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/docs/learn/server-concepts) acts as a proxy between an external service that provides context, data, or capabilities to a Large Language Model (LLM) or AI application. MCP servers connect AI applications to external systems such as databases and web services, translating their responses into a format that the AI application can understand.
### Server Setup
You must [enable MCP servers](https://docs.cloud.google.com/mcp/enable-disable-mcp-servers) and [set up authentication](https://docs.cloud.google.com/mcp/authenticate-mcp) before use. For more information about using Google and Google Cloud remote MCP servers, see [Google Cloud MCP servers overview](https://docs.cloud.google.com/mcp/overview).
### Server Endpoints
An MCP service endpoint is the network address and communication interface (usually a URL) of the MCP server that an AI application (the Host for the MCP client) uses to establish a secure, standardized connection

results.title: Devs guide to MCP Apps in Gemini
results.snippet:
[MCP Apps](https://github.com/modelcontextprotocol/ext-apps) (SEP-1865) solves this. This open Model Context Protocol (MCP) extension pairs a tool with a live UI. In [Gemini Enterprise](https://business.gemini.google/?utm_source=cloud.google.com/blog), that UI renders directly in the chat flow inside a sandboxed iframe, and can expand to fullscreen or a side panel. Edits run locally while the workspace and assistant stay synchronized.
You also avoid rebuilding core foundations: Gemini provides workforce sign-in, governed data access, and the Default Assistant, while you host your MCP server on a private [Cloud Run](https://cloud.google.com/run) service.

Three decoupled tiers work together:
- **Client browser:** Shows the chat alongside the MCP App widget in the side panel.
- **Gemini Enterprise:** The default assistant calls tools, the AppBridge proxy relays widget messages, and the connector manages OAuth.
- **Google Cloud (your project):** You deploy and host the MCP server on Cloud Run, which exposes one JSON-RPC endpoint (/mcp), runs background jobs, and serves the single-file HTML widget.

results.snippet:
# Use the Agent Platform remote MCP server
This document shows you how to use the Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform remote Model Context Protocol (MCP) server to connect with AI applications including Antigravity, ChatGPT, Claude, and custom applications you are developing. The Agent Platform remote MCP server lets you manage Agent Platform resources from your AI application. The Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform remote MCP server is enabled when you enable the Gemini Enterprise Agent Platform API.
[Model Context Protocol](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/docs/getting-started/intro) (MCP) standardizes how large language models (LLMs) and AI applications or agents connect to external data sources. MCP servers let you use their tools, resources, and prompts to take actions and get updated data from their backend service.
## What's the difference between local and remote MCP servers?
- **Local MCP servers** Typically run on your local machine and use the standard input and output streams (stdio) for communication between services on the same device.
- **Remote MCP servers** Run on the service's infrastructure and offer an HTTP endpoint to AI applications for communication between the AI

results.title: Gemini Enterprise release notes
results.snippet:
Support for 3-legged OAuth (3LO) authentication with Agent Identity auth manager for Agent2Agent (A2A) agents is generally available (GA).
This integration lets A2A agents built with the Agent Development Kit (ADK) and deployed on Agent Runtime authenticate to downstream Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers, Google Cloud services, and third-party APIs on behalf of the signed-in Gemini Enterprise user. When a tool requires user consent, Gemini Enterprise automatically prompts the user, validates the callback at `https://vertexaisearch.cloud.google.com/validateUserId`, finalizes credentials with Agent Identity auth manager, and resumes the A2A conversation.

You can configure Virtual Private Cloud (VPC) connectivity for custom Model Context Protocol (MCP) server data stores by routing outbound tool traffic through Agent Gateway (supported in `us-central1` and `europe-west1`). You can host private MCP servers inside your VPC network by using Private Service Connect (PSC) network attachments and agent connectivity templates. You can also route traffic to public MCP servers through Cloud NAT with static external IP addresses for strict IP allowlists.
